items.text: **A light-sound test for the iPad crackle.** Open Battanboo with `?lite` at the end of its address and the three heaviest steady jobs in the sound engine are switched off together: the smoothing on the master (no oversampling), the Air grains, and long reverbs (held to 2 seconds). A line at the top says the test is on. If the crackle stops, one of those three is the cause. Without `?lite`, nothing changes. The buffer test's note now uses the same line at the top.

**Everything Battanboo has to tell you now speaks from the same line at the top.** The small passing messages that sat in the top right corner, warnings (a controller disconnected, something refused), "The sound stopped" with Restart the sound, Reset and Report it, and the error screen (Reload, Report it, Keep going) all open as one line at the top centre, like the update notice; tap it for more, × to close. Report it opens the system check, ready to copy or email. Not shown in audience view or the cinema view.

**The "Performing?" reminder speaks from the top, like the update notice.** It is one line at the top of the screen; tap it for the checklist note, Open the list, Do not remind me or Not now, or close it with ×. Left alone it leaves after 15 seconds. The card at the bottom is gone. Warnings, offers and errors will move to the same place.

**Install Battanboo as an app that works offline.** Battanboo now keeps its own files on the device, so once it has opened once it also opens with no internet: on a Mac from Chrome's install button, on an iPad or iPhone with Add to Home Screen. When you are online it still loads the newest version first.

**Wall and floor now sound different on the grid.** The floor only narrowed left-to-right a little and added a touch of reverb to the top rows, which a single speaker or a Bluetooth box could not reveal. Now the higher a row, the farther away it sounds: softer, darker and wetter, the way distance sounds in a real room. The bottom row stays as it is on the wall. Deep goes further still.

**The grain engine stopped making garbage.** The Air grains made a small new object for every grain (up to 60 a second) and threw it away when the grain ended, and the engine reported in every tenth of a second even when Air was off. An older iPad's sound engine has to stop now and then to clear that rubbish, which can be heard as a regular crackle. Grains now reuse a fixed set of slots and the reports slow down when Air is quiet. They sound the same.

**A second test for the iPad crackle.** Open Battanboo with `?reverb=short` at the end of its address and every reverb is held to 2 seconds, which takes most of the steady work off an older iPad's sound engine. Without it, nothing changes.

**A test for the Bluetooth crackle.** Open Battanboo with `?buffer=steady` at the end of its address and the sound runs on bigger buffers: a little more delay to a touch, more room for a speaker link that hiccups. A note at the top says what the browser gave. Without it, nothing changes.
